<!-- pr-reviewer: 608126a521dbf25b8f40ef567e491889f529eadb -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge** (one non-blocking note on the heavy pin's exactness).

**What looks good**
- The change is minimal and safe: `rings::circle` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/rings.rs`) closes by overwriting the last point with the first, and the first with `start` only when `start` is within 1e-9 mm of the circle. This is a snap of existing points, not an added segment. It moves a point by at most 1e-9 mm (about 5000x under the 0.005 mm verify tolerance), so cleared area and engagement are unchanged, and the crossing law (`guard`) is untouched, so a plan that really crosses itself still falls back by name.
- Other callers (`grow.rs:177`, `troch_plan.rs:212/242`, `mod.rs:410`) all pass a start that is on the circle or get the same exact-close; no behaviour change beyond the ulp.
- No unwrap/expect/panic added; provenance and decision file (`docs/decisions/980-bore-hsm-plan.md`) present; no build.rs/.github/scripts/dependency change; no golden or snapshot PNG changed; files stay under 400 lines.

**Local results** (macOS arm64, trial-merged with upstream/main 3e9b8ae1, clean merge)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| motion lib (debug) | 190 passed, 1 ignored |
| adaptive_orbit_seam (new) | 1 passed |
| adaptive_hsm / adaptive_band / rotary_adaptive / trochoid_slot (debug) | 1 / 2 / 2 / 10 passed |
| release `--ignored`: adaptive_hsm | 5 passed |
| release `--ignored`: rotary_adaptive | 3 passed (incl. r6.2 neck levels refused by name, unchanged) |
| release `--ignored`: motion lib `adaptive` | 1 passed |
| clippy motion + app `--all-targets -D warnings` | clean |
| release `--ignored` app pocket3d_hsm bore test | assertions up to line 109 pass (no level falls back, verifies clean, no budget note); the final exact count pin fails here, see note 1 |

Plan choices vs upstream/main: the only change is the intended one, Z 20 and Z 10 of the user's bore go from Offset rings back to the HSM plan. The 60x14 slot, 60x40 island, trochoid band and r6.2 rotary levels did not flip (all their suites pass unchanged). No gouge/verify verdict changed.

**Overlap**: `git merge-tree` of this head with #953 (grow.rs) and #1007 (hsm.rs notes) is clean for both.

**Requested before merge**: none.

**Notes (not blocking)**
1. The exact pin `(16197, 15458, 1581)` (`crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:118`) does not reproduce on macOS arm64: I measured 16160 / 15432 / 1571 on the PR head (and on the merged tree), with `fell` empty. upstream/main already drifts on this machine too (6503 / 6467 / 222 against the pinned 6500 / 6464 / 222), so this is the same platform float knife edge that #1014 addresses with ranges. Suggest the pin take a range (e.g. moves within a few percent, arcs within a band) like #1014 rather than exact counts, and keep `fell.is_empty()` as the real guard. Whichever of #1014 / this merges second will need to reconcile these lines.
2. Nice that the Z 10 center outline fixture makes the seam testable in debug (~3 s here).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 608126a521dbf25b8f40ef567e491889f529eadb -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

High-tier review (toolpath generator, safety floor). Trial-merged with `origin/main` (3e9b8ae1 plus the commits since) in a fresh worktree: merges cleanly, head verified `608126a5`.

### What looks good
- **The diagnosis holds.** `guard::scan` skips only *consecutive* segments of one walk (`s.1.abs_diff(t.1) <= 1`), so segment 0 (start -> orbit point 1) and segment 96 (orbit's closing vertex -> first spiral point) are tested against each other. With the closing vertex exactly on the start, `orient(c, d, a)` and `orient(a, b, c)` are exactly 0 and `proper` is false. With it ~1e-15 off, both values are ulp-sized with arbitrary sign, and the strict `> 0 / < 0` test can read a proper crossing. That is the reported false positive.
- **The crossing law is untouched.** `guard.rs` is not in the diff. Its `a_figure_eight_crosses_and_a_spiral_does_not` unit test still proves a real crossing is reported, and `pocket_hsm.rs:56` still names the fallback ("crosses itself at ...").
- **The fix is minimal and bounded** (`rings.rs:203-224`). Radius, direction and vertex count are unchanged. The first point moves only when the start is within `ON_CIRCLE` = 1e-9 mm of the circle, and then by at most 1e-9 mm. The last point is overwritten in place, not appended, so no extra vertex and no zero-length segment appear. Every caller works:
  - start far from the circle (`grow.rs:177`, `troch_plan.rs:242`): no snap, and the last point equals the projected first point;
  - start at the centre (`pocket_hsm.rs:254`, `helix_r` 0): no snap, and the orbit is not walked;
  - `rr` 0 / tiny: same as before (degenerate chords that `scan` already filters at 1e-12);
  - NaN: the `<=` is false, so there is no snap and the behaviour is as before.
  
  No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside tests.
- **The new pins are real.** I reverted `circle` locally to main's body, without committing:
  ```
  the_users_z10_bore_level_keeps_its_hsm_plan ... FAILED
  ["adaptive: the HSM plan for this area crosses itself at (-2.09, -0.13); a trochoid its medial line is degenerate - Offset rings cut this pocket instead"]
  ```
  Restored, it passes. The fixture's origin is stated in the test header: a dump of the Z 10 centre area of our own `testdata/models/Milling-test.step` through the 3-D ladder. Nothing third-party.
- Decision file, `Changelog:` line, `Fixes #980`, a conventional subject (`fix(adaptive): ...`) and tests inside `crates/motion` are all present. No goldens changed. No new crate dependency, no process files.

### Local results (merged with main)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --tests` (debug, 68 binaries incl. lib unit tests, `adaptive_orbit_seam`, the `pocket3d_hsm` debug twin) | 714 passed, 0 failed, 48 ignored |
| app `pocket3d_hsm` (debug) | 1 passed, 1 ignored (the heavy pin) |
| app `golden_cl` | 25 passed |
| app `conformance` | 6 passed |
| heavy pin, release, run 1 | ok, 191.7 s - `moves 16197 planar 15458 arcs 1581` |
| heavy pin, release, run 2 | ok, 190.0 s - `moves 16197 planar 15458 arcs 1581` (identical, same notes) |
| `cargo test --release -p camcraft-motion -- --ignored adaptive` | 2 passed (budget fixtures; `adaptive_plans_the_developed_levels_under_the_load_and_kink_laws`) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Is the larger path sound?
16197 moves against 6500 is explained by the notes. Z 20 is back on the HSM spiral with "58 microlift returns (0.3 mm or more over the cleared floor, 945 mm) ... 7 rides on at the floor, 1 retract hops". Z 10 fits 500 arcs where its rings fitted none.

**What I could establish:**
- The path verifies clean against the part solid. `warns` is empty, so there is no gouge and no feed crossing at a depth.
- No budget refusal, and no level falls back.
- The microlift schedule is kept only when its walk on fresh stock reads no worse than the spiral's own engagement bound, and leaves no more than grid crumbs over it (`lift.rs:338-348`). Otherwise the spiral posts as planned, with a note.
- Returns are routed through the cleared area or over the retract plane (`LinkLaw::find` / `high`).
- The HSM levels are the planner's normal output, with its engagement/kink laws. Before this fix the two rings levels were the ones without that guarantee: the first ring slots full width.

**What I could not establish without a machine or simulation:**
- Measured per-level engagement and residual stock on *this* part. The heavy pin asserts verification and counts, not per-level load. The load and break laws are asserted on the motion debug twin's fixture, not the STEP bore.
- That a microlift never brushes uncut stock. This rests on the planner's raster law, not on an independent stock simulation.

Neither is a regression from this PR. Both were equally unproven for the HSM levels that already planned.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (non-blocking)
1. The unit pin `rings::tests::the_orbit_closes_on_its_own_start...` trips on its first assert (exact closure) on main's code. So it proves the closure, not the crossing. The integration fixture is what proves the crossing. That is fine; it is just a weaker pin than its name suggests.
2. Heavy pin and #1010 / fork PR #1014: the pin is still one exact `assert_eq!` with no per-OS slot or comment. A macOS run will need the cfg slot #1014 proposes. It is not blocked by this PR, but #1014 will conflict on these lines and must re-measure from 16197 / 15458 / 1581.
3. The Z 20 note reports "up to 0.32 mm corner scallop ... left for the finishing pass". That is expected roughing behaviour of the load-holding corner rounding, now visible again because Z 20 is back on HSM.
4. `adaptive/mod.rs` stays at 431 lines (untouched). `rings.rs` grows to 259, under the limit.
5. A residual, not this PR's scope: `guard::proper` stays exact-sign. Any other near-shared vertex (not just this seam) could still read an ulp as a crossing. The decision file records why the law was not loosened. If another level shows a sub-micron "crossing", the source of the noise should be fixed the same way.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: f9a9ba871261d99ffb18575d2175059f817065a2 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a read-only re-check of the test-only delta since my review at `608126a5`. I read it with `gh` only and built nothing; the author reports the heavy pin passing in release on this head (16197 / 15458 / 1581).

1. **No planner code changed.** The new head adds a merge of `main` (parents `608126a5` and `3e9b8ae1`, which is current `main`) and commit `f9a9ba87`. That commit touches only `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs` and `docs/decisions/980-bore-hsm-plan.md`. The PR's own diff is still the same 5 files. `rings.rs`, `adaptive_orbit_seam.rs` and the fixture have the same blob SHAs as the reviewed head.
2. **Windows loses nothing.** On Windows x86_64 the pin is still exact: `got == (16197, 15458, 1581)` inside `assert!`. It is no longer `assert_eq!`, but the failure message prints `got`.
3. **Safety assertions still run on every platform.** No warnings (`warns.is_empty()`), no budget note and `fell.is_empty()` sit above the delta, unchanged and outside any `cfg`.
4. **The `cfg` cases are right.** `bore_path_matches` uses `cfg!(all(target_os, target_arch))` in an if / else-if / else chain. The cases cannot overlap and together cover every target. The band applies only when neither Windows x86_64 nor macOS aarch64 matches. The band (16100..=16260 / 15380..=15520 / 1560..=1600) covers both measured triples.
5. **The platform difference is stated plainly.** The test comment says the planner's output differs between platforms and that #1010 owns making it bit-stable. The decision file says the same, and records why a single band (#1014's form) was dropped.

Note (non-blocking): fork PR #1014 will conflict on these lines and can take this form as is.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
